sermon.title: The Founding Fathers Called for Morality
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that the Declaration’s “laws of nature and of nature’s God” mean the Bible’s God, that rights come from the Creator, and that America’s failures on Indians and slavery betrayed those truths. He applies two biblical classes and ways to today’s parties, sexual culture, Court decisions and calls the founding fathers’ demand for morality.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Unverified: 40% unwed births; “six by eight” group claim. Sensitive: Trail of Tears/Jackson, slavery, Democrats/socialism, same-sex marriage/SCOTUS, child-sex agenda allegation, Satan’s kingdom. Overlaps short clip laws-of-nature content.

faqs.question: Was Jefferson a Christian according to critics he cites?
faqs.answer: They said he was not a Christian man, yet the Declaration uses God and Creator language.

faqs.question: What is the first use of God in the Declaration?
faqs.answer: Nature’s God who entitles them—gives authority to separate.

faqs.question: What did Blackstone say about natural law?
faqs.answer: When the Supreme Being formed the universe he established certain laws; man must conform to his Maker’s will, called the law of nature.

faqs.question: Where do unalienable rights come from?
faqs.answer: Endowed by their Creator—second use of Creator language in the Declaration.

faqs.question: What does he say about the Trail of Tears?
faqs.answer: Indian lands taken and sold; Trail of Tears picture—they had no constitutional rights as he recounts.

faqs.question: Did Jackson defy the Supreme Court on Indian rights?
faqs.answer: He says the Court said Indians had a right to stay; President Jackson would not listen.

faqs.question: Is America a democracy or a republic?
faqs.answer: He says it is a republic—representatives carry out what people want—not democracy as majority rule.

faqs.question: What percent of children does he say are born to unwed mothers?
Are Bible believers a minority?
faqs.answer: He says they are a majority yet told to shut up with restricted speech, Bible, prayer and Jesus’ name.

faqs.question: How many ways does he say there are?
faqs.answer: Two ways—right and wrong; your choice if it doesn’t line up to the Bible is wrong no matter how strongly you believe it.
